I am an older man farming in the Somalie lowlands, and the rains here are not always kind. My maize plot is small, only a quarter hectare more or less, and I have planted it with beans between the rows so that if one crop fails I still have something to eat. I do not have cash to spend on fertilizer from the cooperative, and the dealers are far from here anyway, but I will spread the manure from my animals on the field like I always do. I will work this plot with my family — my sons help me weed when the grass comes up — and I keep my own seed from last year's harvest because the improved seed is expensive and not always suited to our dry weather.
